This course provides an overview of the sound system of Spanish. Specifically, the aim 
is to study the principle differences between English and Spanish phonology in order to 
inform the language practitioner as to the best practices for teaching Spanish pronunciation 
to second language learners. To this end, the course will cover the articulation of Spanish 
sounds and how to transcribe them, the principle phonological processes of Spanish, and the 
dialectal variation of the Spanish speaking world. The course also provides an introduction 
to the acoustic analysis of speech sounds and how it can be used to assess progress in 
the L2 classroom. Upon completing the course, students will demonstrate knowledge of the best 
practices for utilizing pronunciation exercises as a supplement to their language lessons.
